paper_metadata.title: Re enhancement effects: Development of a ReaxFF NiAlRe reactive force field for Ni-based superalloys

evidence.quote: A reactive metallic force field, ReaxFFNiAlRe-S23, has been developed to simulate the mechanical behavior of Ni-Al-Re systems.
we developed a reactive metallic force field, ReaxFF NiAlRe-S23, specifically tailored for Ni-Al-Re alloys, parameterized from a comprehensive DFT dataset.

Ni-based superalloys are the materials of choice for commercial turbine blade materials due to their exceptional strength, oxidation resistance, and resistance to gas corrosion at temperatures ranging from 650 to 1000 ◦C [1].
Thus, ReaxFF NiAlRe-S23 is suitable to be applied to study Ni-Al-Re superalloy.
ReaxFF NiAlRe-S23 predicts the formation energies quantitatively well on both Re-containing Ni and Ni3Al systems compared with the DFT results.

Mottura et al. suggested that Re atoms, when positioned near dislocation cores, can impede dislocation movement by obstructing the climb/glide processes during creep, thereby enhancing the alloy's mechanical properties [11].
This improvement is attributed to Re's ability to induce localized atomic disorder, effectively resisting dislocation propagation under external deformation.

mechanisms.name: dislocation pinning
mechanisms.material_state: Ni/Ni3Al interface-dislocation model with Re at dislocation core

evidence.quote: Specifically, adding Re atoms near the dislocation core significantly improves tensile strength while the Re atoms located near the interface has little effect. This suggests that a dispersed distribution of Re atoms within the Ni matrix can hinder the propagation of dislocations under load, thereby increasing tensile strength.

mechanisms.name: solid-solution strengthening

evidence.quote: The addition of Re atoms resulted in improvements in both tensile strength and the associated strain. To further understand the mechanism behind the increase in tensile strength due to Re addition, the microstructural evolution of ID-(4Re0 10Re1)Dis during the tensile process was also examined.

evidence.quote: Our simulations support the mechanism of dislocation hindrance by Re through local disorder transitions, rather than through interface strengthening.
